style: Say in a relaxed, friendly way, like a kind dad helping with homework
lines: Pick a problem. Tap neighbors to read their views.
Views are ready. Tap Make the play, or keep reading.
Tap Add character. Pick two or three neighbors for your play.
Now choose who or what is in their way. That's where the drama comes from.
Tap a backdrop.
Pick a speaker and line. Tap Add line for each scene.
Fix the crossed plan check.
Those puppets only agree. Tap Characters to give them a clash.
Plan checks pass. Tap Perform.
Pick a role. Tap Curtain, then Next line.
That's your line. Read it out loud, then tap Next line.
Your play is finished. Write your closing answer.
Tap Add character to choose one more neighbor. A play needs at least two characters.
Choose a fix, then tick who it helps.
Read the bubble aloud. Use Next line with Space or Enter, or tap it.
Tap Bow to finish your play. Then write what it says about this neighborhood.
Write your closing answer.
Tap three different neighbors to open their views. Then tap Make the play.
Pick a speaker and line, or type one. Tap Add line.
Choose a speaker and line, or type your own. Tap Save line to replace this line.
This scene has six lines. Tap Edit on a script line to change it, or remove a line to make room.
Choose a character card to edit. Tap Build the theater when ready.
Watch this six-second preview. Then tap Characters to give someone a character blocker.
Tap a backdrop to change your stage.
Choose a left wing and a right wing.
Tap a prop to add it. Drag it on stage, or use arrow keys.
Pick a character. Tap up to two costume pieces.
Tap a selected costume piece to take it off. Then choose another piece.
